Minimal scientific simulator testing whether an agent that can revise its representation recovers better after a world shift than an agent limited to parameter updates.
Source explicitly says v0 is not an AGI simulator or proof of the full framework; it isolates representation-evolution behavior.
Source-described environment uses y=a*v*(1+z), with visible variable v and context variable z.
Phase 1 holds z=0 so a simple linear representation is sufficient; Phase 2 varies z so the old representation becomes insufficient.
State-only baseline is described as y_hat=theta*v and may update theta but not representation.
REE maintains an active hypothesis and can compare h0=a*v, h1=a*v+b*v*z, and h2=a*v+phi(v,z).
REE is described as able to change dimensionality and causal structure of its representation rather than merely adjust coefficients.
Persistent error/torsion above threshold triggers an offline sleep cycle that generates candidate hypotheses.
Source describes candidate evaluation on held-out data with complexity penalty; evidence is intended to compare generalization rather than only fit.
Source states a candidate should commit only if it significantly improves generalization.
Named metrics are post-shift MSE, recovery time, accepted representation changes, false mutation rate, representation complexity and compute.
REE is predicted to show lower post-shift error, faster recovery and sparse accepted representation changes when fixed observations are insufficient.
If the predicted pattern occurs, source says representation change can be modeled as a controlled/testable process rather than unconstrained self-modification.
Version 0 intentionally tests only a narrow representation-evolution claim and does not establish the full CTRE framework.
Dataclass state contains velocity and context floats.
Environment stores change_point and internal timestep t.
Reset sets t=0 and returns LatentState(velocity=1.0, context=1.0).
Phase is 0 before change_point and 1 at/after change_point.
Phase 0 context is constant 1.0; Phase 1 context is sampled uniformly from 0.5 to 2.5.
Target is 2*velocity in phase 0 and velocity*context in phase 1.
Observation exposes velocity, context, target and phase; next state retains velocity with sampled context; reward is negative absolute prediction error.
Hypothesis dataclass carries name, operator and integer complexity.
augment transform returns velocity, context and a newly sampled Gaussian random scalar.
Null candidate preserves the active operator and complexity.
Interaction candidate uses operator interaction and complexity active+1.
Augment candidate uses operator augment and complexity active+1.
State-only learner has a fixed representation and may update parameters but cannot change its feature space.
Initializes learning rate, two zero weights and error history.
Prediction is dot product of two weights with fixed features.
Performs online gradient-like update weights += lr*(y-y_hat)*x and logs absolute error.
Returns mean recent absolute error or infinity before observations.
Reports representation complexity as number of weights, fixed at two for this class.
REEAgent is a minimal representation-evolving learner whose active feature transformation may change after persistent failure.
Initializes lr, torsion_threshold, min_memory=50, linear active hypothesis complexity 1, two zero weights, error/violation/memory stores, generator, innovation log and mutation_count=0.
Default linear feature vector is [1.0, velocity].
Interaction feature vector is [1.0, velocity, velocity*context].
Augment delegates to hypothesis.transform and prepends intercept 1.0.
Prediction is dot product of active-hypothesis features and current weights.

Computes prediction error, pads weights if feature dimensionality grew, performs lr*error*x update, logs absolute/squared errors and memory sample, then may invoke sleep_cycle if torsion trigger fires.
Stores squared errors and truncates to most recent 100.
After min_memory, trigger is mean of last 20 absolute errors > torsion_threshold.
Uses last 100 memory samples and candidates from HypothesisGenerator; returns empty list before min_memory.
Null candidate score is negative mean absolute residual over sampled memory.
Interaction score is correlation between residuals and velocity*context, or zero when residual standard deviation is zero.
Returns candidates as (hypothesis, score) tuples sorted descending by score; augment candidates are not scored by the implemented branches.
If best candidate differs from active hypothesis and mutation_count is zero, sleep_cycle commits it internally, increments mutation_count and clears violation_history.
Changing hypothesis reinitializes/pads weights according to operator and logs old/new hypothesis plus error-at-mutation.
Internal automatic commit is limited to one mutation by mutation_count==0 guard.
Offline evaluator asks whether failures are explainable by fixed observational interface or whether a new representation improves fit with complexity control.
Evidence dataclass stores baseline_error, candidate_error, improvement, complexity_cost, intervention_gain and passed.
Chronologically splits data at train_fraction (default .7) into train and validation subsets.
Uses np.linalg.lstsq; if residual array is nonempty returns its mean, otherwise computes mean squared prediction error.
Base features are [1,v]; contextual features are [1,v,v*context].
Builds target and baseline/candidate matrices from validation_data; interaction and augment candidates both use contextual features, while null uses base features.
Returns an Evidence object carrying the calculated fields.
Resets environment, repeatedly calls env.step(state), records observation/target pairs and does not assign returned next_state back to state.
Collects phase-0 batch and trains StateOnlyAgent by repeated online updates.
Collects phase-0 batch and directly fits REE's current [1,v] linear weights while appending error/memory, without calling normal update/sleep logic.
Pretrains 100 steps, then executes 5000 env steps and StateOnlyAgent updates, collecting errors; returned next_state is not assigned.
Pretrains 100 steps, creates OfflineEvaluator, then executes 5000 env/agent updates while collecting errors and an offline_evaluations list.

When agent.should_sleep() and enough errors exist, last 100 memory samples are split and candidates=agent.sleep_cycle() is iterated through evaluator.evaluate; evidence is logged and passed candidates may be committed.

Post-shift error is mean of last 200 errors; recovery is first post-change rolling 50-step mean <=0.1; innovation_count is innovation-log length; false_mutation_rate is 0 if any innovation else 1; final complexity comes from active hypothesis.
Seeds NumPy with 0, uses change_point=2500, StateOnlyAgent lr=.02 and REEAgent lr=.02/torsion_threshold=.5.
Runs state baseline and REE on separately created ToyEnvironment instances sequentially under the same global NumPy RNG stream.
Prints both metric dictionaries and offline evaluations.
Executable assertions require REE post-shift error < state post-shift error and REE recovery time <= state recovery time; then print 'Assertions passed'.
